*Manage a local Traefik stack from Codex or Claude through its external tk CLI.*

> **Never operate a stack inferred from the plugin cache; resolve an explicit or verified stack and use its external tk CLI.**

## Why install this

Keep the operating instructions with your other skills while the CLI, Compose
configuration and application data stay in their own repositories. Both hosts use
one skill and one local stack binding. A compatibility check catches an older CLI
before the agent tries a service operation.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/traefik/SKILL.md` | Shared Codex and Claude operating instructions. |
| `skills/traefik/scripts/traefik.js` | Stack discovery, local binding and CLI compatibility checks. |
| `skills/traefik/references/operations.md` | Command selection, failure handling and ownership boundaries. |
| `skills/traefik/evals/` | A real CLI contract, replay output and an incompatible-contract trap. |

## Quick start

Claude Code — run in chat:

```text
/plugin marketplace add natejswenson/claude-skills
/plugin install traefik@claude-skills
/traefik
```

Use `/traefik:traefik` if Claude displays the plugin-qualified command. For a local
development checkout, register its absolute path as the marketplace source instead.

Codex — run in a terminal from this repository's root:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
codex plugin add traefik@claude-skills
```

Start a new Codex session, then invoke in chat:

```text
$traefik
Check my Traefik stack and verify local-memory connectivity.
```

With the skill loaded, ask to bind your Traefik checkout as the default. For manual
setup, run from the directory containing the loaded `SKILL.md`:

```bash
node scripts/traefik.js bind --stack /absolute/path/to/traefik
node scripts/traefik.js detect
```

Replace the example path with your actual stack checkout. Binding first verifies
its external CLI. Updating a plugin never copies or updates that CLI.

## Triggers

- "check Traefik health"
- "diagnose local HTTPS or DNS"
- "show service logs"
- "preview a rebuild"
- "remove a service"

## Requirements

- **Claude Code:** Local file/shell tools, Node 18+, and an external stack with
  executable `scripts/tk`. No app connection is needed for stack operations.
- **Codex:** The same runtimes and CLI, with normal sandbox approval for Docker or
  host networking where required. Claude app/MCP connections are not imported.
- **Personal data:** Both hosts share `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/traefik-skill/settings.json`,
  containing only a schema version and the selected absolute stack path. The file
  is mode 0600. Compose files, `.env`, certificates, vaults and Docker data remain
  outside the plugin. Local-memory integration uses the host's existing opt-in and setup.

The external [traefik-local-cli](https://github.com/natejswenson/traefik-local-cli)
must support `tk capabilities --json` with agent protocol 1 and the capabilities
listed in [operations.md](skills/traefik/references/operations.md). The old display
version alone is insufficient. Its runtime needs Python 3 and Docker Compose;
capability detection itself does not need the Docker daemon.

See [Codex migration notes](../../docs/codex-migration.md) for host tool handling.

## Ownership and migration

The marketplace owns the shared skill and its manifests. The CLI owns executable
stack operations. Each local stack owns routing, certificates and private settings.
Resolve helper paths from the loaded skill, never the current working directory;
resolve stack operations from the helper's selected stack, never the plugin cache.

After verifying the plugin in a fresh session, retire any old repository-local
`traefik` skill or loose user-level `tk` skill to avoid competing copies. Preserve
the external `traefik-onboard` workflow; this plugin reads its stack-specific
instructions for new applications.

## Development

```bash
cd skills/traefik/skills/traefik
npm test
```

Tests are offline and use temporary stack fixtures. The baseline replays a real
capability response; its trap removes a required capability. See
[baseline.md](skills/traefik/references/baseline.md) before refreshing it.
From the repository root, run `python3 tools/sync_codex.py --check` and
`python3 tools/check_compatibility.py` to verify both host manifests.
